n77c31b49766.s: Loans and advances given by the Union Government to States are classified as:
n77c31b49766.x: Loans and advances to States change the Government's financial assets, so they are capital expenditure. Maintenance of assets and interest payments are revenue expenditure.

nindian-economy-46-3.s: Capital expenditure strengthens long-term productive capacity mainly because it:
o: Meets the recurring running costs of government
Is directed at acquiring, creating, upgrading or extending the life of assets
Covers salaries, pensions and interest payments
Is given as grants to States for their schemes
nindian-economy-46-3.x: Capital spending buys, creates, upgrades or extends the life of assets, which builds long-term capacity. Running costs, salaries, interest and grants to States are revenue expenditure.

n2d2e9eee598.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the shares of Union Budget 2026-27 expenditure?
o: States' share of taxes is the largest item at 22 per cent
Central Sector Schemes take 17 per cent
Defence takes a larger share than interest
n2d2e9eee598.x: Defence takes 11 per cent, well below interest at 20 per cent. The order is States' share of taxes 22, interest 20, Central Sector Schemes 17 and defence 11 per cent.

nindian-economy-62-15.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's external debt?
o: It is borrowing from external or foreign sources
It may involve foreign currency obligations
Most of it is owed by the Government (sovereign debt)
'India's External Debt: A Status Report' is published by the Department of Economic Affairs
nindian-economy-62-15.x: Most of India's external debt is non-sovereign, owed by companies and banks; government external debt is only about 2.6 per cent of GDP. The other statements are correct.

nd83207ba9be.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about off-budget borrowing?
o: The Food Corporation of India borrowed from the NSSF to cover unpaid food subsidy
Budget 2021-22 ended the FCI-NSSF arrangement and brought food subsidy on-budget
Loans raised by government entities and serviced from the budget are counted in the fiscal deficit
Off-budget borrowing hides the true level of debt
nd83207ba9be.x: Off-budget loans are serviced from the budget but are kept outside the fiscal deficit - that is why they are called off-budget. The other statements are correct.

nindian-economy-59-12.s: Money held by the Government of India in trust is kept in the:
nindian-economy-59-12.x: The Public Account holds money in trust. The Consolidated Fund is the main account, the Contingency Fund meets urgent needs and the NIF has a permanent corpus.

new.s: The Plan and Non-plan classification of expenditure ended with which Union Budget?
new.x: The Plan/Non-plan split ended with Budget 2017-18, at the end of the 12th Plan; 2016-17 was the last Budget to use it.

new.s: Which committee (2011) called the Plan/Non-plan split of expenditure 'dysfunctional'?
new.x: The C. Rangarajan Committee (2011) called the split dysfunctional and an obstacle to outcome-based budgeting.

new.s: After the Plan/Non-plan split ended, Union expenditure is classified mainly as:
new.x: The Plan/Non-plan split was replaced by the revenue vs capital classification.

new.s: Which of the following is a developmental expenditure?
new.x: Irrigation and flood control is developmental; defence, pensions and interest payments are non-developmental.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a non-developmental expenditure?
new.x: Medical and public health is developmental expenditure; interest, pensions and administrative services are non-developmental.

new.s: Grants given by the Union to States, even when used to create assets, are classified as:
new.x: Grants to States are revenue expenditure even if assets are made; loans to States are capital expenditure.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about expenditure classification:
1. Food and fertiliser subsidies are revenue expenditure.
2. Repayment of loans is revenue expenditure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Subsidies are revenue expenditure. Repayment of loans reduces a liability, so it is capital expenditure.

new.s: The Peacock-Wiseman hypothesis was based on public expenditure data of:
new.x: Peacock and Wiseman (1961) studied UK data and found spending rises in steps (displacement effect).

new.s: Wagner's law is also known as the law of:
new.x: Wagner's law, that spending rises faster than national income as an economy industrialises, is the law of increasing state activity.

new.s: In Union Budget 2023-24, major subsidies took what share of every rupee spent?
new.x: Major subsidies took 7 per cent in 2023-24 BE (6 per cent in 2026-27); 9 per cent is a common wrong figure.

new.s: Union total expenditure in Budget Estimates 2026-27 is about what share of GDP?
new.x: Total expenditure of ₹53,47,315 crore is 13.6 per cent of GDP; revenue expenditure alone is 10.5 per cent.

new.s: Effective capital expenditure equals capital expenditure plus:
o: Grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets
new.x: Effective capex = capital expenditure + grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets; ₹17.15 lakh crore (4.4 per cent of GDP) in 2026-27.

new.s: Food and fertiliser subsidies together form about what share of the Union subsidy bill in 2026-27?
new.x: Food (₹2,27,629 crore) and fertiliser (₹1,70,799 crore) make up 87 per cent of the ₹4,54,773 crore subsidy bill.

new.s: Which of the following is an explicit subsidy?
new.x: Interest subvention appears as a budget line, so it is explicit; under-pricing of education, health and irrigation water are hidden subsidies.

new.s: Under-recoveries of oil companies after the Oil Pool Account closed were later paid through:
new.x: After the Oil Pool Account was closed on 1 April 2002, under-recoveries were paid through oil bonds.

new.s: Who chaired the Expenditure Reforms Commission set up in 2000?
new.x: K.P. Geethakrishnan chaired the Expenditure Reforms Commission (28 February 2000); Bimal Jalan chaired the 2014 Expenditure Management Commission.

new.s: Who was the first President of the BRICS New Development Bank (2015)?
new.x: K.V. Kamath was the first President of the New Development Bank, not Bimal Jalan.

new.s: In the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27, which is the correct order of expenditure by size?
o: Capital outlay > Revenue expenditure > Loans and advances
Revenue expenditure > Loans and advances > Capital outlay
Revenue expenditure > Capital outlay > Loans and advances
Loans and advances > Capital outlay > Revenue expenditure
new.x: AP spends most on revenue expenditure (about 83 per cent), then capital outlay, then loans and advances.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's capital outlay in Budget Estimates 2026-27 is about:
new.x: AP's capital outlay is ₹48,698 crore (+47 per cent) in BE 2026-27; ₹33,135 crore was 2025-26 RE and ₹16,141 crore 2024-25.

new.s: Which of the following is a non-marketable instrument of the Centre's internal debt?
new.x: NSSF special securities are non-marketable internal debt; G-Secs, T-Bills and Cash Management Bills are marketable.

new.s: Gross market borrowing of the Centre budgeted for 2026-27 is about:
new.x: Gross market borrowing is ₹17.20 lakh crore in 2026-27; net borrowing is ₹11.73 lakh crore.

new.s: Which currency had the largest share in India's external debt at end-December 2025?
new.x: The US dollar had 54.8 per cent, the rupee 30.1 per cent and the yen 6.3 per cent - not all debt is in dollars.

new.s: Which is the largest multilateral lender in India's external debt?
new.x: The Asian Development Bank is the largest multilateral lender with 32.8 per cent.

new.s: India's external debt at end-December 2025 was about what share of GDP?
new.x: External debt was USD 765.5 billion, 20.4 per cent of GDP, at end-December 2025 (18.4 per cent at end-December 2024).

new.s: If the interest rate (r) exceeds the growth rate (g), keeping debt-GDP stable requires:
new.x: When r > g, a primary surplus is needed; when g > r, the debt-GDP ratio falls on its own.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the FRBM (2018) debt targets:
1. General government debt target is 60 per cent of GDP.
2. The Centre's share of it is 40 per cent and the States' 20 per cent.
3. They followed the N.K. Singh Committee (2017).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The FRBM (2018), following the N.K. Singh Committee (2017), set general government debt at 60 per cent: Centre 40 and States 20.

new.s: The Centre's debt-GDP ratio in Budget Estimates 2026-27 is about:
new.x: The Centre's debt-GDP is 55.6 per cent in BE 2026-27; it peaked at 61 per cent in 2020-21.

new.s: States raise market borrowings mainly through:
new.x: Under Article 293 States borrow only within India, through State Development Loans (SDLs).

new.s: The Public Debt Management Cell (PDMC), set up in 2016, is located in the:
new.x: The PDMC (2016) is in the Department of Economic Affairs, headed by the Joint Secretary (Budget), not in the RBI.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about public debt management:
1. The RBI manages government debt under the RBI Act, 1934.
2. A statutory Public Debt Management Agency was set up after the 2015-16 Budget.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The RBI manages debt under the RBI Act, 1934. The statutory PDMA was proposed in 2015-16 but not created.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's off-budget borrowing in March 2023 was about:
new.x: AP's off-budget borrowing was ₹1.28 lakh crore (9.7 per cent of GSDP) in March 2023.

new.s: In Western usage, deficit financing means:
o: Only borrowing from the central bank
Any financing of a budget deficit, mainly by borrowing from the public
Printing currency to pay for imports
new.x: In the West it means any financing of a budget deficit, mainly market borrowing; in India it means borrowing from the RBI.

new.s: Deficit financing in the Second Five Year Plan amounted to about:
new.x: Deficit financing in the Second Plan was about ₹1,100 crore against ₹1,200 crore planned.

new.s: In which Five Year Plan was reliance on deficit financing to be strictly limited?
new.x: The Third Plan said reliance on deficit financing would be strictly limited.

new.s: Which of the following is part of the Centre's 'other liabilities' and not internal debt?
new.x: State Provident Funds sit in the Public Account as other liabilities; market loans, T-Bills and NSSF securities are internal debt.

new.s: Market loans make up about what share of Andhra Pradesh's debt?
new.x: Market loans are about 75 per cent of AP's debt.

new.s: Ad hoc Treasury Bills, now abolished, were a device for:
o: Automatic RBI financing of the government
new.x: Ad hoc Treasury Bills gave automatic RBI financing to the government; they were replaced by Ways and Means Advances.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about methods of deficit financing?
o: Borrowing from the RBI monetises the deficit
Ways and Means Advances are temporary advances from the RBI
An OMO sale of G-Secs adds liquidity
Ad hoc Treasury Bills have been abolished
new.x: An OMO sale of G-Secs drains liquidity; a purchase adds it. The other statements are correct.

new.s: The RBI-Government agreement that began phasing out ad hoc Treasury Bills was signed in:
new.x: The September 1994 agreement began the phase-out; the March 1997 agreement ended ad hoc T-bills.

new.s: From which date was the RBI barred from subscribing to primary issues of government securities?
new.x: Under the FRBM framework the RBI was barred from primary issues from 1 April 2006, though the FRBM Act is of 2003.

new.s: Since the 2018 FRBM amendment, monetised borrowing from the RBI is allowed only:
o: Up to 3 per cent of GDP
new.x: Since 2018 monetised borrowing is allowed only on escape-clause grounds, with the slip capped at 0.5 per cent of GDP.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT inflationary in its effect?
new.x: Repayment of debt withdraws money from the economy, so it is not inflationary; creation of new money is the most inflationary.

new.s: Of every rupee spent in Union Budget 2026-27, interest payments take about:
new.x: Interest takes 20 paise of every rupee spent, about 40 per cent of revenue receipts.
